_note_fetch_family: FETCH FAMILY POPULATION (Issue #301, POC-A2.1/2) — 26 cards the clause KIND already supported, authored as compendium ENTRIES rather than machinery. Every printed effect below was read off `tools/meta_tracker/cards.json` (the engine's own all_card_data dump), never memory. VOCABULARY ADDED HERE, on top of `_note_fetch`'s fields. Targets: `stage1` / `stage2` (the printed stage), `tera`, `pokemon_ex` (an ex-rule body: ex or Mega ex), `item` / `tool` / `stadium` (each a strict subset of the existing `trainer` class), `any` (a dig with no class restriction at all). Fields: `amount` = the printed cap on cards THIS clause may take, ABSENT MEANING ONE (so the three missing-amount fixes below stay bug-fixes instead of making an absent field ambiguous), with the explicit sentinel `"all"` for an unbounded 'any number of'. `choice` = true when the clause is ONE ALTERNATIVE of a single choice ('...or...', 'up to N in any combination of X and Y'): the card's true cap across its `choice` clauses is the MAX of their amounts, NEVER the sum — Max Rod takes 5 cards total, not 5 Pokemon AND 5 Energy. Absent means an independent leg whose amount ADDS (Dawn genuinely fetches a Basic AND a Stage 1 AND a Stage 2 = 3 cards). `dig_from` = `top` (default) | `bottom` (Dusk Ball looks at the BOTTOM 7). `name_family` = the printed NAME restriction, RECORDED VERBATIM AND UNDECIDED — `fetch_closure.fetch_target_matches` refuses such a clause for REACH rather than ignoring the field (ignoring it would read Hop's Bag as fetching any Basic), and the four carriers are ruled `partial` for exactly that (Issue #306 cross-post: `card_text.name_in_family` is the string half of the key, but the missing piece is a build-time index over the pool keyed by family; and note 1134's restriction is a SUBSTRING test, not the owner prefix the other three use, so one oracle cannot be assumed). Rider `discard_remainder` = the dug cards NOT taken go to the DISCARD (Explorer's Guidance) instead of being shuffled back. `trigger: on_attach` = the fetch fires when the card is ATTACHED from hand (Telepath Psychic Energy), joining on_evolve / on_bench_play / on_attack. NOTE `dest` absent means HAND — `_note_fetch` said 'deck (default)', which was a doc slip: no committed entry ever meant it and nothing reads the field. THE 26, each with its printed effect. 1125 Master Ball: a Pokemon -> hand. 1082 Hyper Aroma: up to 3 Stage 1 -> hand. 1115 Hop's Bag: up to 2 Basic Hop's Pokemon -> Bench. 1126 Precious Trolley: ANY NUMBER of Basics -> Bench. 1127 Tera Orb: a Tera Pokemon -> hand. 1132 Team Rocket's Great Ball: a Trainer -> hand. 1134 Team Rocket's Transceiver: a Supporter with 'Team Rocket' in its name -> hand. 1101 Call Bell: a Supporter -> hand, going-SECOND first turn only. 1109 Miracle Headset: up to 2 Supporters from DISCARD -> hand. 1205 Cyrano: up to 3 Pokemon {ex} -> hand. 1210 Brock's Scouting: up to 2 Basics OR 1 Evolution -> hand (two `choice` clauses). 1220 Team Rocket's Proton: up to 3 Basic Team Rocket's Pokemon -> hand. 1233 Canari: up to 4 {L} Pokemon -> hand, gated on discarding another card (`cost: discard_1`). 1077 Roto-Stick: top 4, any number of Supporters. 1094 Bug Catching Set: top 7, up to 2 in any combination of {G} Pokemon and Basic {G} Energy. 1102 Dusk Ball: BOTTOM 7, a Pokemon. 1185 Explorer's Guidance: top 6, take 2, DISCARD the rest. 1193 Hassel: top 8, up to 3, only if one of my Pokemon was KO'd during the opponent's last turn. 1231 Dawn: a Basic AND a Stage 1 AND a Stage 2. 1092 Secret Box: an Item AND a Tool AND a Supporter AND a Stadium, gated on discarding 3 (`cost: discard_3`). 1194 Colress's Tenacity: a Stadium AND an Energy. 1215 Ethan's Adventure: up to 3 in any combination of Ethan's Pokemon and Basic {R} Energy. 1238 Tarragon: up to 4 in any combination of {F} Pokemon and Basic {F} Energy, from DISCARD. 1184 Lana's Aid: up to 3 in any combination of no-Rule-Box Pokemon and Basic Energy, from DISCARD. 19 Telepath Psychic Energy (Special): provides {P}, and ON ATTACH to a {P} Pokemon searches for up to 2 Basic {P} Pokemon -> Bench. It carries TWO type gates and they are different questions: `energy_type: 5` is what may be FETCHED (Basic {P} Pokemon) and `target_type: 5` is the {P} RECIPIENT the attach must be made to for the fetch to fire at all — the same field name, and the same meaning, `accel` already uses for a restricted recipient (1146 Wondrous Patch), so this is one vocabulary rather than a second one. Without `target_type` the clause set would miss a printed restriction and the card would owe a `partial`. It is also the first card to carry BOTH kinds, so note the two spell a colour differently and deliberately: `energy_provide` names it as the string `type` (card 17 Ignition Energy's precedent, `_note_misc`) while `fetch` names its lock as the numeric EnergyType — each field belongs to its own kind's vocabulary, and unifying them is a change to card 17's committed clause, not to this entry. 1206 Larry's Skill: a Pokemon AND a Supporter AND a Basic Energy — authored, but `partial`: 'Discard your hand' is the card's whole cost and no clause field carries it (the 1192 precedent). ONE CARD IS DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED: 1188 Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking (4 copies, `slowking`) — 'search your deck for 2 cards ... then put those cards ON TOP of it'. `dest` has no such value and `deck_odds` has no notion of a KNOWN TOP, so it stays REFUSED and is cross-posted to Issue #289 (T3.5/11), which owns that concept; 4 copies in a shipped deck is the concrete reason that issue matters. It is one of the TWO fetch-family sites the census still reports; the other is 173 Noctowl's on-evolve Jewel Seeker Ability, which is outside this Trainer/Energy batch (0 copies, 0.00 meta). ON `covers` AND UNREAD FIELDS: a verdict is a statement about whether the CLAUSE SET describes the whole printed effect, NOT about whether a consumer reads every field of it — `amount` has no reader today (`combat._hand_yield_units` says so in as many words, and the reach graph asks only 'can this card find X at all'). So Buddy-Buddy Poffin is `full` because its clauses now say 'up to 2', and wiring a transition that spends that 2 is T4's job, not a reason to under-declare the data. _note_stadium: STADIUM clauses (Issue #304, POC-A2.1/6). TWO kinds, not one: `stadium_static` (an ongoing board modifier while the card is in play) and `stadium_trigger` (fires on a board EVENT). A single `stadium` kind was declined because the 22 pool Stadiums are five unrelated effect shapes wearing one card type, so one kind would be a union of everything or a lie. The write is carried by the clause's `effect`, not by its kind — 1120 Crushing Hammer's `coin` shape — and every write-set is declared in common/snapshot_coverage.CLAUSE_WRITES. What EVERY Stadium does (replace the one in play, spend the once-per-turn allowance) is STRUCTURAL and lives in apply_option's `_PLAY` footprint instead of here: rulebook L135-137 'Only one Stadium can be in play at a time—if a new one comes into play, discard the old one and end its effects', L112/L138 'only one Supporter card and one Stadium card per turn'. FIELDS: `effect` = hp_delta | damage_reduction | damage_boost | prevent_damage (static) / damage_counters (trigger); `amount` = the magnitude, SIGNED (Gravity Mountain is -30); `applies_to` = the body predicate, and WHICH body it binds to is fixed by the effect (the modified body for hp_delta, the DEFENDER for damage_reduction/prevent_damage, the ATTACKER for damage_boost, the body just benched for damage_counters); `symmetric: true` = 'both yours and your opponent's', which every one of these prints; `timing` = before_/after_weakness_resistance where the card says so; `source` = whose attack the modifier keys on; `on` = the trigger EVENT, deliberately NOT the `trigger` key, which routes a clause to a SITE (on_evolve / on_bench_play / on_attach / on_attack) and would file a Stadium's clause on an option the engine never poses for it. _note_playability_gate: THE `cost_required` RULING (Issue #372, POC-A2.1/3d) — read this beside `_note_draw`, which minted the field and is the reason it was applied unevenly. `cost_required` says failing to pay `cost` makes the card UNPLAYABLE, which is a different fact from the cost merely being expensive. `_note_draw` authored it on 1187 Morty's Conviction, 1208 Iris's Fighting Spirit and 1200 Kofu because those were among Issue #302's 14 partial DRAW clauses; the three FETCH cards printing the SAME restriction were not in that issue's scope and so were never looked at. The result was one store holding two opposite readings of one sentence: 1233 Canari and 1187 print *"You can use this card only if you discard another card from your hand."* character for character and disagreed. Issue #302 even quotes *"the `cost` field exists (Ultra Ball's discard_2)"* as its example of the field that already existed, without ever asking whether Ultra Ball's own sentence was a gate. The prose here had already reached the right reading while the DATA lagged — this file's `_note_fetch_family` writes Canari as *"gated on discarding another card"* and Secret Box as *"gated on discarding 3"*, and 1233's `_covers` reason said *"the cost the card is gated on"*. A SECOND SUBSYSTEM HAD ALREADY RULED IT, independently and in the opposite direction from this store, which is the strongest evidence in the issue: the cgpy twin encodes playability as a `legal` predicate, and `src/cgpy/defs/generated_chains.json` gives 1233 Canari `legal: [{op: handOthers, n: 1}]` — seeded automatically by `tools/parity/seed_chains.py`'s rule `R-T08`, which regexes this very sentence at BUILD time — while `src/cgpy/defs/chain_overrides.json` gives 1121 Ultra Ball a HAND-AUTHORED `legal: [{op: handOthers, n: 2}]`. `cgpy/chain.py` checks it live (*"discard-cost needs n OTHER hand cards"*). So the twin engine refused an unpayable Ultra Ball while this compendium priced it as merely expensive. Note the scope of the neighbouring claim in `_note_fetch` that nothing *"parses card text at runtime OR build time"*: that is true of the COMPENDIUM and must not be widened to the repo — `R-T08` is exactly such a build-time parser, for the twin. THE RULE, stated once so the halves cannot drift again: a `cost` carries `cost_required: true` IF AND ONLY IF the card prints a restriction on PAYING THAT COST, in either of the two forms the pool prints — *"You can use this card only if you discard/put..."* (1092, 1121, 1148, 1187, 1208, 1233) or the parenthetical inverse naming the same payment, *"(If you can't put 2 cards FROM YOUR HAND on the bottom of your deck, you can't use this card.)"* (1200 Kofu). It is deliberately NOT 'prints a playability restriction', which is wider and would be wrong three separate ways, each a real card here: (a) ten cards print *"You can use this card only if..."* about the BOARD rather than a payment — 1101 Call Bell's *"only if you go second"*, 1201 Briar's *"only if your opponent has exactly 2 Prize cards remaining"*, 1080, 1098, 1108, 1193, 1217, 1228, 1234, 1240 — and those take a `condition`; (b) 1079 Rare Candy and 1230 Grimsley's Move print *"You can't use this card during your first turn"*, a TURN restriction in the same words; (c) 1239 Naveen prints *"(If you can't DRAW any cards in this way, you can't use this card.)"* — Kofu's exact sentence SHAPE, but the inability is about the effect succeeding and Naveen's discard is *"you MAY discard any number"*, optional. None of the three carries a `cost` today, but Issue #302 names Naveen's optional pre-discard as its one unmodelled leg, so the day that leg is authored a loose reading would demand the flag on a card whose gate is not about paying. `tests/cards/test_card_effects.py` grades the biconditional against the engine's own card text on every run, in BOTH directions, and asserts all three near-misses as exclusions rather than merely describing them. NOW GATED, this issue's change: 1121 Ultra Ball (`discard_2`), 1092 Secret Box (`discard_3`, on all four legs beside the cost), 1233 Canari (`discard_1`). DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, and the reason recorded because a sweep over 'every card with a cost' would wrongly catch them: 1192 Carmine (*"Discard your hand and draw 5 cards."*) and 1206 Larry's Skill (*"Discard your hand and search your deck..."*) print an INSTRUCTION, not a restriction. Discarding your hand is always payable — including on a hand holding nothing but the Supporter itself, which discards to nothing and still resolves — so `cost_required` there would assert a playability restriction the card does not print. WHY IT MATTERS even though nothing reads the field today (`apply_option()` raises NotImplementedError; T0 freezes the contract): at T4 this is a LEGALITY error and not a pricing one. An Ultra Ball held with a 1-card hand is not a cheap Ultra Ball, it is not a legal play, and pricing it as merely expensive puts an ILLEGAL option on the menu with a positive delta — worse than the silent zero this compendium exists to prevent, because a silent zero prunes a real option while this offers an unreal one. Exposure is the reason it was worth doing now rather than at T4: 17 copies of Ultra Ball across five of our six decks, plus 2 of Secret Box. DEFERRED, named so it is not conflated: 1148 Blowtorch prints *"You can use this card only if you discard a Basic {R} Energy card from your hand."* and has NO entry in this file at all, so there is no `cost` for the flag to ride. Ruling it needs a cost value that does not exist — a TYPED, single-card discard — and minting one is a `CLAUSE_WRITES` decision rather than a data edit. 0 copies across our six decks, so nothing is mispriced meanwhile, and the test above holds the deferral as a TRIPWIRE rather than a TODO: the moment 1148 gains a `cost`, the biconditional grades it.
_note_draw: DRAW clauses, the CONDITIONAL half (Issue #302, POC-A2.1/3). The 14 draw Supporters whose committed clause was a FLAT count where the printed card is conditional — the worst-served family in docs/plans/apply-seam-coverage.md. Every one of the 14 was PROBE-MEASURED, not authored: `classify_effect_clauses` counts the actor's DRAW logs, and the header of card_effects.py already says a conditional count 'resolves to the best OBSERVED case', so a long game that organically hit Lacey's prize-bonus mode measured 8 and shipped 8. That is why these are overrides now: a measurement of one resolution cannot state a card whose count depends on the board. Every printed text below was read off `tools/meta_tracker/cards.json` (the engine's own all_card_data dump), never memory. THREE NEW SHAPES, each because a real card needs it and nothing more. (1) `to_hand_size: N` — 'Draw cards until you have N cards in your hand' is a REFILL, not a draw-N: the count depends on the hand at resolution, so it is mutually exclusive with `amount` rather than an alias for it (1239 Naveen 5, 1216 Team Rocket's Ariana 5/8, 1208 Iris's Fighting Spirit 6, 1203 Surfer 5). (2) `amount_if: {condition, amount|to_hand_size}` — '...draw 6 cards. If X, draw 8 INSTEAD' is two magnitudes and a board predicate, and the second REPLACES the first rather than adding to it. Shape copied from 17 Ignition Energy's shipped `amount` + `amount_on_evolution` rather than inventing a third convention, generalised so the branch names its predicate instead of hard-coding one (1227 Lillie's Determination, 1199 Lacey, 1181 Billy & O'Nare, 1216, and 1214 Emcee's Hype, which is the same shape and the same predicate as Lacey and therefore cannot hold the opposite verdict in the same store). New predicates, all NESTED inside `amount_if` and so never seen by `planner._condition_holds`, which evaluates only a TOP-LEVEL `condition`: `exactly_6_prizes_remaining`, `opp_3_or_fewer_prizes`, `hand_size_10_plus_after_draw` and `all_own_pokemon_team_rocket`. `hand_size_10_plus_after_draw` is deliberately NOT spelled `hand_size_10_plus`: Billy & O'Nare prints 'Draw 2 cards. THEN, if you have 10 or more cards in your hand, draw 2 more', so the predicate is about the hand AFTER the base draw and a reader testing the pre-play hand would be off by two in the direction that fires the bonus when it should not. (3) `cost` + `cost_required: true` — the `cost` field already exists (1121 Ultra Ball's discard_2); what was missing is that a cost can make the card UNPLAYABLE, which is a different fact from it being expensive. `cost_required` says the card cannot be played at all unless the cost is paid (1187 Morty's Conviction, 1208, 1200 Kofu). New cost values: `discard_hand` (1192 Carmine, and 1206 Larry's Skill, which prints the SAME sentence and was ruled partial for exactly the lack of this field — repeated on all three of its legs, which is 1092 Secret Box's shipped shape for one cost paid once across a multi-leg find) and `bottom_2` (Kofu). TWO NEW RIDERS, both declared in common/snapshot_coverage.CLAUSE_WRITES and both NONDETERMINISTIC: `shuffle_own_hand_in` (the ONE-SIDED refresh — `shuffle_both_hands` minus the opponent legs, and a separate key because `common/strategy/refresh.py`'s ADR-0060 oracle splits on exactly that distinction) and `both_hands_to_bottom` (Lucian puts both hands on the BOTTOM rather than shuffling them in). THE COIN CARDS KEEP `kind: draw`, NOT `kind: coin`, and the reason is mechanical rather than aesthetic: `_union_overrides` replaces measured clauses BY KIND, so a `coin`-kinded override would leave the probe-measured `draw` clause standing beside it and the compendium would claim the card draws twice. The coin therefore rides as `amount_if: {condition: coin_tails}` — the heads leg is the base `amount`, the tails leg replaces it — and both cards stay `partial` regardless, per the standing ruling that a coin stated as a certainty needs an `Expectation` and not a scalar (1120 Crushing Hammer). THE SYMMETRIC LEG IS OUT OF SCOPE AND SAID SO: 1213 Judge, 1080 Unfair Stamp, 1223 Harlequin and 1237 Lucian all shuffle and redraw the OPPONENT's hand, which needs a `state_value` term that prices their hand and which the seam already refuses as an accepted POC unknown. All four carry their OWN leg exactly and stay `partial` naming the opponent one — four silent errors turned into four declared ones. Then, flip a coin. If heads, you draw 5 cards, and your opponent draws 3 cards. If tails, you draw 3 cards, and your opponent draws 5 cards.' 1237 Lucian: 'Each player shuffles their hand and puts it on the bottom of their deck. (If you can't draw any cards in this way, you can't use this card.)' — refill carried, the OPTIONAL pre-discard of any size is not, so partial. 1192 Carmine: 'If you go first, you may use this card during your first turn.
